```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
# Bash chunks are a record of commands you ran in the Terminal. Knitting shows
# them but doesn't run them again.
knitr::opts_hooks$set(engine = function(options) {
```

Notes for [Workshop 2](https://mb5370.bioinformatics.guide/workshop2.html). Run the commands for this workshop in the Terminal, from inside the folder named under each heading. Copy each command you run into a bash chunk.

## Redbean assembly

Commands run in `redbean/`.
```{bash}
cd ~/mb5370-workshops/redbean
pwd

cat /pvol/data/amtp4/*_[012].fastq > amtp4.fastq 
wtdbg2 -x ont -g 5m -t 4 -i amtp4.fastq -fo amtp4
wtpoa-cns -t 4 -i amtp4.ctg.lay.gz -fo amtp4.ctg.fa

#takes 48.554b sec

assembly-stats amtp4.ctg.fa #is a command-line tool that reports summary statistics for a genome or sequence assembly. sum: total length of all contigs in bases (roughly your assembly size)1.n: number of contigs; 2.ave: average contig length; 3.largest: length of the longest contig; 4.N50: the contig length at which contigs of that size or longer cover at least 50% of the total assembly. Higher N50 generally means a more contiguous assembly. The n beside it is how many contigs it takes to reach that 50%; 5.N60, N70...: the same idea at other cutoffs; 6.N_count / Gaps: number of ambiguous N bases and the gaps they form (usually 0 for contigs, higher for scaffolds)

cat /pvol/data/amtp4/*.fastq > amtp4_20x.fastq #20x coverage
wtdbg2 -x ont -g 5m -t 4 -i amtp4_20x.fastq -fo amtp4_20x
wtpoa-cns -t 4 -i amtp4_20x.ctg.lay.gz -fo amtp4_20x.ctg.fa
#221.286 sec
assembly-stats amtp4_20x.ctg.fa 
```


## Flye assembly

Commands run in `flye_genome/`.
```{bash}
cd flye_genome
#Make symbolic links to the same raw data we used for redbean
ln -s ../redbean/amtp4.fastq .
ln -s ../redbean/amtp4_20x.fastq .

#running flye in a smaller dataset in the background. Open a new empty shell script. save in flye_genome

#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --time=60
#SBATCH --ntasks=4 --mem=10gb

echo "Starting flye in $(pwd) at $(date)"

flye --nano-raw amtp4.fastq --out-dir amtp4 --genome-size 5m --threads 4

echo "Finished flye in $(pwd) at $(date)"

#Once you have saved your slurm script you can submit it to the queue using the sbatch command
sbatch run_flye_small.sh
squeue #check status

#new file in flye_genome;It shows output from the flye command as it is running
tail slurm-326.out

#If you want to follow (-f) the output as it is created use
tail -f slurm-326.out

#running flye on the larger dataset
sbatch run_flye_large.sh
squeue

tail slurm-327.out
tail -f slurm-327.out
```


## Assembly graphs with Bandage
#checked assembly_graph_amtp4.gfa: zoomed in on highly connected region - edge_15 has a depth of 42x

#checked assembly_graph_amtp4_20x.gfa: chromosome is the large circle, 24x, plasmid is teh smaller circle, 23x. The repeat is the short segment in the big circle at 208x. Compared to the low coverage graph, the main change is that the tangle has been resolved into 2 clean closed circles. More reads-the assembler could bridge the gaps through ambiguous regions.
## Assembly quality with QUAST

Commands run in `quast/`.
```{bash}
cd ~/mb5370-workshops/quast
pwd
#use this command to look at the contig sizes in the flye assembly
cat ../flye_genome/amtp4_20x/assembly.fasta | bioawk -c fastx '{print $name, length($seq)}' | sort -n -k2
#Two largest contigs: contig_10(3378345) & contig_59 (1775300)
#Extracting them 
samtools faidx ../flye_genome/amtp4_20x/assembly.fasta contig_10 contig_59 > flye_asm/vibrio.fasta

#repeating for redbean assembly
cat ../redbean/amtp4_20x.ctg.fa | bioawk -c fastx '{print $name, length($seq)}' | sort -n -k2
##longest contigs: ctg2    1764934 & ctg1    3343987
samtools faidx ../redbean/amtp4_20x.ctg.fa ctg1 ctg2 > redbean_asm/vibrio.fasta

#creating a link to the original reads
ln -s ../flye_genome/amtp4_20x.fastq .
##also for the reference assembly
ln -s /pvol/data/amtp4/reference/vibrio .


#run quast
quast -o quast_vibrio redbean_asm/vibrio.fasta flye_asm/vibrio.fasta -L -t 4 --circos --glimmer -r vibrio/vibrio.fna --features  vibrio/vibrio.gff --nanopore amtp4_20x.fastq
```
